# Implementation Plan for DASL Microservice Test Browser

## Overview

This plan outlines the approach to build a plugin-based microservice test suite for various DASL dag-cbor parser implementations across languages.

Each implementation exposes a systemd service with a nix flake and HTTP web service interface, returning test results including CAR files (CID, dag-cbor), timing, and perf data.

The goal is to create a unified test browser and control plane that can dynamically select any implementation, invoke tests, and display results in a grid of tiles representing each plugin.

## Key Components

### 1. Language Microservices

- Provide existing implementations as independently deployable systemd-managed services.
- Each service exposes unified HTTP JSON/CBOR API endpoints for decode, encode, roundtrip, batch testing.
- Support performance tracing and CAR output generation.

### 2. Plugin Selector & Dispatcher

- A central control service or CLI that lists available microservices/plugins.
- Enables invoking tests on any or all selected plugins.
- Collects and aggregates results and performance profiles.

### 3. Tile-Based Web Interface

using @dasl/tiles 
see ~/projects/dasl/IMPL/users/atproto/atproto_repos/
dasl-tiles/
webtil.es
atmosphere-browser
jakesimonds_jklb-social

for package.json   "@dasl/tiles": "^1.1.3"


- A web UI showing interactive tiles per implementation plugin.
- Each tile shows test status, recent performance stats, crash counts.
- Provides controls to trigger tests, view logs, and explore CAR artifacts.

### 4. Integration with dasl-testing

- Test results collected feed into dasl-testing unified reports.
- Crash reproducers and fuzz test inputs auto-imported into fuzz harnesses.
- Performance data aggregates into DASL-wide analysis dashboards.

## Implementation Steps

1. Audit existing language services for HTTP API compatibility and systemd integration.
2. Design a plugin registry format to describe available implementations and endpoints.
3. Build a plugin selector component capable of dispatching requests and collecting results.
4. Design and implement the tile-based frontend UI for test browsing and triggering.
5. Update dasl-testing report generation to include plugin test status.
6. Automate fuzz and crash repro testing from findings through the microservices.
7. Document usage, deployment, and development workflow.

## Timeline & Milestones

- Phase 1: Microservice audit and HTTP API harmonization (1 week)
- Phase 2: Plugin selector service and dispatcher implementation (2 weeks)
- Phase 3: Tile-based UI frontend development (3 weeks)
- Phase 4: Integration with dasl-testing reports and automation (2 weeks)

## Dependencies

- Existing nix flakes and systemd services for each implementation
- dasl-tiles web interface codebase
- dasl-testing and fuzzing infrastructure


---

This plan can be used to guide the development of a robust cross-language DASL microservice testing ecosystem.
